::: {#fig-essential-supremum-norm}

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}

### R

```{r}
#| label: essential-supremum-norm-r
#| fig-alt: >-
#|   Plot of a function on x from 0 to 1. A solid blue diagonal line rises
#|   from an open circle at the origin to the point 1 at x of 1.
#|   A single vermilion filled point sits far above, at the value 5 at x of 0.
#|   A dashed horizontal line at height 1 marks the essential supremum.
#| fig-height: 3.5
#| fig-width: 5
esn_x_pf <- seq(0, 1, length.out = 101)
esn_line_pf <- tibble::tibble(x = esn_x_pf, y = esn_x_pf)
esn_open_pf <- tibble::tibble(x = 0, y = 0)
esn_spike_pf <- tibble::tibble(x = 0, y = 5)
esn_aes_pf <- ggplot2::aes(x, y)
ggplot2::ggplot(esn_line_pf, esn_aes_pf) +
  ggplot2::geom_line(colour = "#0072B2") +
  ggplot2::geom_point(data = esn_open_pf, shape = 1, size = 3) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(data = esn_spike_pf, colour = "#D55E00", size = 3) +
  ggplot2::geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed") +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "s", y = "f(s)")
```

### Python

```{python}
#| label: essential-supremum-norm-python
#| fig-alt: >-
#|   Plot of a function on x from 0 to 1. A solid blue diagonal line rises
#|   from an open circle at the origin to the point 1 at x of 1.
#|   A single vermilion filled point sits far above, at the value 5 at x of 0.
#|   A dashed horizontal line at height 1 marks the essential supremum.
#| fig-height: 3.5
#| fig-width: 5
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

esn_x_pf = np.linspace(0, 1, 101)
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5, 3.5), layout="constrained")
ax.plot(esn_x_pf, esn_x_pf, color="#0072B2")
ax.plot(0, 0, marker="o", markerfacecolor="white", color="black")
ax.plot(0, 5, marker="o", color="#D55E00")
ax.axhline(1, linestyle="dashed", color="black")
ax.set_xlabel("s")
ax.set_ylabel("f(s)")
plt.show()
```

:::

The function in @exm-essential-supremum-norm:
$f(s) = s$ except $f(0) = 5$.
The supremum is $5$, reached only at the single point $s = 0$,
which has [measure zero](#def-measure-zero),
so the essential supremum norm is the dashed height $1$.

:::
